refs.note: Pitch-matched to cello-freesound-alt (measured -19 semis from A3). D2 was tried first (per the stated pitch-match plan) but the automated YIN F0 detector mismeasured it at -7 semis (148.6Hz, an octave-error artifact of a weak/missing fundamental on that stopped note -- both stereo channels independently show ~73Hz as a real but much weaker peak beneath a dominant 148Hz 2nd harmonic). C2, the open string, has a strong clean fundamental and measures reliably at -21 semis, 2 semitones from the target -- the closest reliable match available on this instrument.
128 kbps MP3 preview from freesound's CDN, NOT the lossless original; HF above ~14 kHz is codec-limited, so treat noise-floor / flatness / air-band metrics from this reference as unreliable.

Each renders through its own drum-gen recipe (drum-open-hihat, drum-tom-high, drum-tom-low) distinct from the covered closed-hihat and single-tom clips -- an open hi-hat, a higher-pitched tom, and a lower-pitched tom are each a real acoustic sound, so hihat-vcsl/tom-vcsl are not valid ground truth for them despite the shared instrument family. tom-lofi's drum-tom-low recipe itself is a plain lower tom with no bitcrush stage, but the SHIPPED instrument is not plain: its DefaultFX chain adds a 5-bit bitcrusher plus a 2kHz lowpass, so a future reference for it needs to match that lo-fi/filtered character, not the bare recipe's output. No isolated recording of an open hi-hat or a differently-pitched tom was found in VCSL beyond the single hi-hat and tom already catalogued, nor among the local freesound absorptions. Drop one into $BEATMO_WAV_REFS/sources and `make refs-adopt` it.

Pitch-matched to harp-freesound-alt (measured +22 semis from A3). G5 (the theoretically exact match) was tried first, but this specific VCSL sample (both f1 and mf1 velocity layers) makes the automated YIN F0 detector report an octave-down 390Hz/+10 semis, even though independent FFT inspection of the same sustain window shows the true fundamental is genuinely ~780Hz/G5 (a closely-spaced detuned-unison triplet around 778/781/783Hz likely fools YIN into a subharmonic lock). Neighbouring notes E5 and B5 do not exhibit this bug and measure cleanly; E5 (+19, 3 semitones from target) is closer than B5 (+26, 4 semitones) and was kept. Was harp-vcsl (A4, +12 semis); renamed to keep the id honest about the note.

Pitch-matched to piano-grand-freesound-alt (measured +22 semis from A3). VCSL only samples this Steinway B at whole-tone intervals (A#,C,D,E,F#,G# per octave), so no exact G5 sample exists; F#5 (-1) and G#5 (+1) are the neighbours. Measured F#5=740.4Hz (+21) vs G#5=829.6Hz (+23) -- G#5 is the closer match in cents (0.80 semis from target vs 1.17 for F#5) and was kept. Was piano-grand-vcsl (A#0, -23 semis); renamed to keep the id honest about the note.

Baritone saxophone, NOT the alto that `sax` models: different horn/range/timbre from sax-A4 (Iowa MIS alto sax; 4 semitones higher F0). There is no `sax-baritone` builtin instrument id, so this is filed under `sax` as a second, lower-register real-audio reference rather than left orphaned. `refs candidates -instrument sax` will show a pitch-spread warning between this and sax-A4 — that is expected: judge recording quality (room tone, mic distance, articulation) here, not timbre parity with the alto. 128 kbps MP3 preview from freesound's CDN, NOT the lossless original; HF above ~14 kHz is codec-limited, so treat noise-floor / flatness / air-band metrics from this reference as unreliable.
